title: Lara Croft Was Almost a Male Indiana Jones Clone
hook: In 1996 Eidos budgeted for 100,000 copies of Tomb Raider, a game whose hero started out as a male Indiana Jones clone until the boss feared a lawsuit. It sold more than seven million, and this week Lara turned 30. Would you have played Tomb Raider with a male lead?

script: Did you know Lara Croft was almost a man? In the mid nineties, a small studio called Core Design in Derby, England started work on a new three dimensional adventure game. Artist Toby Gard's first design was a male hero exploring tombs. Studio boss Jeremy Heath-Smith took one look and said no. The character looked far too much like Indiana Jones, and he feared the studio would get sued. So Gard went back to the drawing board and came back with a woman. She was first named Laura Cruz, a South American adventurer. The team then made her a British aristocrat and changed Cruz to Croft. Laura became Lara partly because Americans struggled to say the name. Eidos boss Ian Livingstone has said the company budgeted for around one hundred thousand copies. Tomb Raider launched on the Sega Saturn in October nineteen ninety six and went on to sell more than seven million copies. In two thousand ten, Derby even named a stretch of its new ring road Lara Croft Way after a public vote. This week the series turned thirty, and Amazon Games dropped a new teaser for Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, which reimagines the original Lara. That new game is dated for February twelfth of two thousand twenty seven across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch and PC. Follow for more gaming history.
